data.body: Fixes bug B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run: the load-based worker clamp gave the lock holder 1 worker; the holder should get a floor of workers (ci.suite_min_workers) so it does not hog the host-wide lock. Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run --regression-test <test>`.
data.title: Fix bug B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run: suite lock held for hours by a full suite at pytest -n 1

data.text: Fix B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run and the listed ci-infra bugs one at a time, each fully gated and merged (lead brief to fx-ci-infra)

data.claim: workers.compute clamps floor(cores*0.75-loadavg) to min_workers=1 even for the lock holder, so a loaded host yields -n 1
data.falsifier: compute with load*cores > cores*high returns >1 for a holder
data.mechanism: ci._execute calls _with_workers/localize_hooks after SL.hold with no holder floor
data.probe: pytest tests/test_auto_workers.py -k holder on unfixed code
data.probe_output: TypeError: compute() got an unexpected keyword holding_suite (4 failed on unfixed)
data.question: Why did the suite-lock holder run at -n 1?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED: holder gets -n 1 under load; regression tests fail on unfixed code
reviewed r-small-files/r-everything-configurable: new knob ci.suite_min_workers with upgrade note; files <20KB; no hardcoded tunables

chunk_findings.detail: `holding_suite` is derived from `local`, but `local` is true for any locally executed run, not only for the full-suite lock holder. A local selected-test run (`scope.scope == "selected"` and `local=True`) on a loaded host can have its worker clamp computed as 1 worker, yet `_with_workers(..., holding_suite=local)` and `localize_hooks(..., holding_suite=True)` raise it to `ci.suite_min_workers` (default 8). That bypasses the load clamp even though the selected run does not hold the host-wide full-suite lock described by the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:553-557

chunk_findings.detail: The new `holding_suite` flag is wired to the pre-existing `local` argument: `_with_workers(cmd, cfg, used, "command", holding_suite=local)` and `localize_hooks(..., holding_suite=True)` under `if local`. `local` controls whether pre-commit localisation happens, not whether this run holds the host-wide full-suite lock. Given `_prepare(local=True)` for a `scope` where `scope.scope == "selected"` (a selected run that holds no suite lock), the command is resolved with the holder floor and can overcommit the host; given a full-suite lock holder invoked with `local=False`, the command can still be clamped to `-n 1`, leaving B-suite-lock-held-by-n1-run unfixed on that path. The condition should be an explicit lock-holder flag, not `local`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_prepare

chunk_findings.detail: `_under_memory_pressure` floors the high-memory halving at `lo`, not at the suite-holder floor `held`. Given a suite-lock holder with `min_workers=1`, `max_workers=16`, `suite_min_workers=8`, `workers="auto"`, and a high load that the load clamp would otherwise reduce below 8, `compute` first produces `n=8` via the new floor. If memory pressure is high but not critical (for example `free=0.10`, so `pressure=0.90` with the default high mark `0.85`), this line returns `max(1, 8 // 2) = 4`, silently dropping the holder below `suite_min_workers`. That can recreate the original suite-lock-hogging condition; only the critical-memory case is covered by the new test, so this high-memory bypass is uncaught.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest shows the actual full-suite pytest command path was also changed in `ddflow/services/ci.py` via `_with_workers`, but none of the added tests import or execute that path; every new test calls `WK.compute` or `WK.localize_auto` directly with `holding_suite=True`. If `_with_workers` forgets to propagate `holding_suite=True` into `WK.compute`/`WK.localize_auto`, a busy host still gives the lock holder `-n 1`, while all added unit tests pass. The regression coverage therefore does not exercise the changed integration point most likely to reintroduce the original bug.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_suite_lock_holder_is_not_clamped_to_one_worker (missing integration coverage)

chunk_findings.detail: The test passes both a list-style placeholder, `args: [-n, auto]`, and a string-style placeholder, `x: -n auto`, but only asserts `"-n 8" in text`. A buggy `localize_auto` that replaces only `x: -n auto` and leaves the actual `args: [-n, auto]` unchanged still makes this assertion pass, so the test does not verify the list form provided as input is actually localized to `-n 8`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_localize_auto_gives_the_holder_its_floor

data.summary: A review run killed before its verdict (shell/tool exit) is still charged a round: fix-B-suite-lock... rubber_duck showed 2/4 after one finished review plus one killed mid-flight. An interrupted review that recorded nothing should not consume the budget.
data.title: interrupted review (no verdict recorded) is charged a round

data.body:
Fixes bug Bfdcb5c177c: A review run killed before its verdict (shell/tool exit) is still charged a round: fix-B-suite-lock... rubber_duck showed 2/4 after one finished review plus one killed mid-flight. An interrupted review that recorded nothing should not consume the budget.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bfdcb5c177c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bfdcb5c177c --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bfdcb5c177c: interrupted review (no verdict recorded) is charged a round

chunk_findings.detail: The rename from `_execute(..., local=...)` to `_execute(..., holding_suite=...)` was applied to the definition and to the full-suite call at `ddflow/services/ci.py:422`, but the selected-scope `_prepare` path cited in previous finding 1 is unchanged: it still calls `_execute(..., local=True)` for a run where `scope.scope == "selected"`. Because `_execute` no longer accepts a `local` keyword, that call now raises `TypeError: _execute() got an unexpected keyword argument 'local'` before any selected run can execute. This is not just the original semantic overcommit issue; the selected path is now broken entirely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_prepare

chunk_findings.detail: In `_under_memory_pressure`, the high-memory branch returns `max(held, n // 2)`. For `compute`’s explicit `workers` setting, `n` is not first floored to `held`; the new `held` clamp was only added to the `else`/`auto` branch. Given `cfg.ci.workers="2"`, `min_workers=1`, `max_workers=16`, `suite_min_workers=8`, `holding_suite=True`, `files=10`, and `free=0.10` (`pressure=0.90`, above the default high mark `0.85`), the explicit branch yields `n=2`, then this line returns `max(8, 2 // 2) == 8`. A healthy host returns 2, and a memory-pressured host returns 8, so memory pressure is increasing the worker count; if `suite_min_workers` is intended as a holder floor for explicit settings, the normal-memory explicit path is equally wrong because it never floors to 8.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workers.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The revised probe does not answer prior finding 4: the list-style placeholder `args: [-n, auto]` has been removed, leaving only string-style `-n auto` lines and an exact text assertion. A `localize_auto` implementation that still fails to rewrite list-style placeholders would produce the exact expected text and pass, so the list-style path remains unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_localize_auto_gives_the_holder_its_floor
